name: Optic Disc Pit

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnosis of Optic Disc Pit

criteria.description: Presence of a well-circumscribed, grayish, oval or round depression on the optic disc margin observed on fundoscopic examination
Evidence of serous macular detachment or retinoschisis on optical coherence tomography (OCT)
Fluorescein angiography showing late leakage at the optic disc pit site
Visual field defects consistent with optic nerve involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic optic disc pit on fundoscopic exam plus at least one supportive imaging finding such as OCT or fluorescein angiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not indicated.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital optic disc pit visible on fundoscopic examination

pathognomonic.symptomName: Serous macular detachment associated with optic disc pit

retinal swelling linked to optic disc pit

common.symptomName: Visual field defects including arcuate scotomas
searchTerms: visual field loss including arcuate scotomas

common.symptomName: Decreased visual acuity due to maculopathy
Relative afferent pupillary defect in affected eye
searchTerms: impaired pupil response in one eye
splitting of retinal layers in macula
retinal layer separation in central vision area

occasional.symptomName: Elevated intraocular pressure secondary to associated glaucoma

rare.symptomName: Optic nerve pallor secondary to chronic damage
searchTerms: pale optic nerve due to damage
optic nerve pallor from chronic injury
retina detaching secondary to other eye problems
retinal detachment caused by underlying condition
new abnormal blood vessels in eye causing glaucoma

imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing optic disc pit and associated serous macular detachment or retinoschisis
Fluorescein angiography demonstrating late leakage at the optic disc pit
Fundus photography revealing characteristic optic disc pit morphology
other: Visual field testing showing arcuate scotomas or other defects
Electroretinography may be normal or show mild abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Larger excavation involving the optic nerve head with associated chorioretinal coloboma
Typically more extensive visual field loss
Different fundoscopic appearance lacking the small pit morphology
Funnel-shaped excavation of the optic disc with surrounding pigmentary changes
Usually unilateral and associated with other ocular anomalies

redFlags: Rapid decrease in visual acuity indicating progressive maculopathy
Development of retinal detachment requiring urgent intervention
Elevated intraocular pressure suggesting secondary glaucoma
references: Gass JD. Optic disc pits and associated maculopathy. Am J Ophthalmol. 1969;68(4):618-630.
